title: Push and pop in a linked-list stack
summary: Treat the head node of a singly linked list as the top of the stack so both push and pop operate at the head.
context: On the left is the external stack view, with the top above and the bottom below; on the right is a vertical singly linked list with the head node at the top, the tail node at the bottom, and next arrows pointing downward. A leftward arrow between them is labeled "Implemented with a linked list. Exposes stack operations".
description: The stack top corresponds to the linked list's head node, and the stack bottom corresponds to the tail node. Consequently, the stack order from bottom to top is the reverse of the linked-list order from head to tail. Beside the open top of the stack on the left, the push arrow enters downward and the pop arrow exits upward.
result: In a linked-list stack, both pushing and popping add or remove nodes solely at the head of the linked list, each taking O(1) time.

frames.title: Initial stack: head node 5 is the top
frames.explanation: From bottom to top, the initial stack is [1, 3, 2, 5] with 4 elements; from head to tail, the linked list is 5 → 2 → 3 → 1. Head node 5 corresponds to the stack top, and tail node 1 corresponds to the stack bottom.
frames.key_state: Initial stack (bottom to top) [1, 3, 2, 5]; linked list (head to tail) 5 → 2 → 3 → 1, with head node 5 as the top.
frames.announcement: The initial stack has 4 elements, with linked-list head node 5 at the top and tail node 1 at the bottom.

frames.title: Push 4 at the head of the linked list
frames.explanation: Call push(4), labeled on the right "Add node 4 to the head of the linked list". A cyan new node 4 is inserted above the previous head node 5, with its next pointer pointing to 5, and becomes the new head node. From head to tail, the linked list is now 4 → 5 → 2 → 3 → 1, and from bottom to top, the stack is [1, 3, 2, 5, 4] with 5 elements; the head node and stack top are 4, while the tail node and stack bottom remain 1.
frames.key_state: After push(4): stack (bottom to top) [1, 3, 2, 5, 4]; linked list (head to tail) 4 → 5 → 2 → 3 → 1, with new head node 4 as the top.
frames.announcement: Call push(4) to insert node 4 at the head of the linked list; 4 becomes the new head node and stack top.

frames.title: Pop 4 from the head of the linked list
frames.explanation: Call pop(), labeled on the right "Delete the head node". Remove and return the previous head node 4, making its successor 5 the new head node. From head to tail, the linked list returns to 5 → 2 → 3 → 1, and from bottom to top, the stack returns to [1, 3, 2, 5] with 4 elements; the head node and stack top are 5, while the tail node and stack bottom remain 1.
frames.key_state: After pop() removes and returns head node 4: stack (bottom to top) [1, 3, 2, 5]; linked list (head to tail) 5 → 2 → 3 → 1, with stack top restored to 5.
frames.announcement: Call pop() to remove and return linked-list head node 4, restoring the head node and stack top to 5.
